name: Tekin
old_description: The Tekin Pro-Lock Bullet connectors securely hold your battery connections no matter the conditions. Our proprietary design utilizes a unique internal locking mechanism that holds bullet connections firmly and will not fatigue or loosen up over time. A simple twist of the thumb nut cap, push down and your Pro-Lock bullet unlocks for easy removal from the battery terminal. Easy, tool-less insertion and removal means no more torn up fingers and pulling on wiring to unplug your batteries. Pro-Lock Bullets are the only solution for solid, efficient connections.
about:
Tekin, Inc. operates from McCall, Idaho, where it designs and manufactures electronic speed controls, motors, servos, batteries, and connectors for radio-controlled vehicles. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

Its product line spans multiple categories: the RX8 GEN3 and RSX PRO electronic speed controls for 1:8-scale and modified racing; the RS GEN3 and BXR compact ESCs for crawling and general use; the RX4 rock-racing controller; brushless motors such as the TYPE-D drag motor, Eliminator series, GEN4 and GEN4 SPEC-R lines; brushed crawler motors; Tekin servos with aluminum housings and magnetic encoding; POWER CELL LiHV batteries in 1S–4S configurations; and the proprietary Pro-Lock bullet connectors with a tool-less locking mechanism. The firm also develops the HotWire programming device and firmware for ESC tuning.

Tekin serves competitive racers and hobbyists across several RC disciplines. Its equipment is used in 1:8-scale circuit racing, no-prep drag racing, rock crawling, scale trail driving, and custom adventure builds. The company references top drivers choosing the RX8 GEN3 and drag racers pairing Eliminator motors with V295 firmware.

The company emphasizes a 'built for racers by racers' philosophy, highlighting its proprietary Pro-Lock connector locking mechanism, Active Drag technology for smooth throttle control, Element Proof designs that withstand weather, and Ultra-Low Resistance (ULR) motor windings for higher output. These features are presented as the core differentiators behind its Real Racing Gear branding.

about:
Telink Semiconductor is headquartered in Tustin, California, and was founded in 2014. The company operates as a fabless semiconductor supplier, designing and marketing multi-protocol wireless system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for the Internet of Things. No founder names or ownership structure are disclosed in the available sources.

The company develops SoCs that integrate Bluetooth Low Energy, Bluetooth Classic, Bluetooth Mesh, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Wi-Fi 6, Amazon Sidewalk, and 2.4 GHz proprietary protocols. Product families include the TL323X series for Matter and Amazon Sidewalk, the automotive-grade TL3225 series, the high-performance TL721X series, and the TL3228 targeting 8 KHz wireless gaming peripherals. Telink supports development with software development kits (SDKs), an integrated development environment, hardware design guidelines, reference designs, a product selection tool, and a technical forum staffed by its engineers.

Telink’s solutions are used in smart home devices such as lighting and door locks, wireless audio and gaming accessories requiring low latency, human input devices including keyboards and mice, universal remote controls for major smart TV and set-top box brands, industrial IoT nodes, and electronic shelf labels for smart retail. The company cites deployments with some of the world’s largest smart TV, set-top box, and OTT box manufacturers.

Telink emphasizes ultra-low power efficiency, multi-protocol coexistence on a single chip, and certification to Thread, OpenThread, and Matter standards as key differentiators. It positions its one-stop development ecosystem — silicon, software, tools, and direct engineering support — as a way to accelerate customers’ time-to-market.

name: Terrain Biomedical, Inc.
old_description: Working with the leading brands in our competitive industry, the staff at Terrain Biomedical has been refurbishing and selling quality sterilizers since 2005. Our company has developed a solid reputation as a trustworthy and reliable source of sterilizers and a variety of other medical equipment.
about:
Terrain Biomedical, Inc. is based in Buffalo Grove, Illinois. The company was established in 2005 to provide a cost-effective, full-life-cycle approach to medical equipment transactions. Founded by biomedical engineers who believed clients deserved more than generic sales, the firm began as a refurbisher and seller of sterilizers and has since expanded into a comprehensive resource for equipment acquisition, service, and support.

The company refurbishes, sells, rents, and services a wide range of medical devices, including autoclaves, defibrillators, fetal monitors, patient monitors, electrosurgical units, and surgical tables. Its degreed biomedical engineers follow strict processes to restore used equipment to manufacturer-recommended specifications, performing repairs, preventative maintenance, electrical safety inspections, and operational testing. Terrain also installs equipment, trains staff, consults on equipment planning, and manages equipment removal. The facility handles brands such as Zoll, Corometrics, Mindray, and STERIS, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Terrain serves healthcare providers across the continuum, with a noted focus on skilled nursing and rehabilitation facilities, as well as hospitals and clinics that require reliable, cost-effective equipment solutions. Customers range from individual practices to larger institutions seeking rental programs for emergency or long-term needs, and the company also purchases used equipment directly from facilities.

The firm differentiates itself by emphasizing three pillars: ensuring equipment works, ensuring it is necessary, and ensuring it lasts. Its engineers are qualified to perform repairs and recertifications on behalf of several major manufacturers, and the company offers free white-glove local delivery, a rental fleet for immediate deployment, and a commitment to complete equipment life-cycle management rather than one-time sales.

name: Teton Valley Brands
old_description: We’ve crafted a potato chip made with the best ingredients and 100% Real Idaho® potatoes. The result is an all natural and deep potato-flavored chip. Or, as we like to call them — Real Idaho potato chips.
about:
Teton Valley Brands operates from Caldwell, Idaho, where it produces snack foods using locally sourced ingredients. The company was established to create potato chips made exclusively from Idaho potatoes, though a founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details are not specified, but the business emphasizes its Idaho roots and community-based workforce.

The company manufactures two primary product lines: Real Idaho® Potato Chips and Tallow & Stone tortilla chips. Potato chips are made from hand-selected Idaho potatoes supplied by Cranney Farms, a multi-generational farm in Oakley, Idaho. The tortilla chips are cooked in traditional beef tallow rather than seed oils. Production takes place in a state-of-the-art facility in Caldwell that currently employs ten people, handling the entire process from manufacturing through shipping.

Teton Valley Brands serves retail channels across Idaho's Treasure Valley, with products stocked in stores carrying collegiate-branded chips produced in partnership with Boise State Athletics and the University of Idaho Athletics. The customer base includes grocery retailers and consumers seeking clean-label snacks. The company also works directly with its potato supplier, Cranney Farms, as a strategic partner.

The brand differentiates itself through a simple-ingredient philosophy: all products are gluten-free, non-GMO, and free of artificial colors, flavors, preservatives, hydrogenated oils, and refined salts. The company states that keeping the full production cycle in Idaho—from potato farming to finished packaging—ensures quality and supports the local economy.

name: Texas Instruments
old_description: Texas Instruments (TI) is a semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Texas. Produces analog and embedded processing chips used in a wide range of applications including automotive, industrial controls and consumer electronics.
about:
Texas Instruments traces its roots to 1930 when Geophysical Service Inc., an oil and gas exploration venture, opened in Dallas, Texas. The founders’ entrepreneurial drive led the company into electronics during World War II, and by 1951 it was renamed Texas Instruments Incorporated. Today the business is headquartered in Dallas and operates as a publicly traded semiconductor manufacturer.

TI designs, fabricates, packages, and tests analog and embedded processing chips, offering a portfolio of more than 80,000 products. Its global manufacturing network includes 300 mm wafer fabs that run on 100 % renewable electricity, and the company reports producing tens of billions of chips each year. With roughly 33,000 employees and over 100,000 customers, TI handles everything from process technology and design through final test and delivery.

The company’s components serve automotive, industrial, consumer electronics, communications, data center, personal electronics, and medical equipment markets. Engineers at automakers, industrial automation firms, smartphone makers, and data‑center operators rely on TI’s analog ICs, microcontrollers, and wireless transceivers for applications ranging from vehicle electrification to AI‑driven servers.

TI says its founding purpose was to make electronics more affordable through semiconductors, a mission that still guides its three core ambitions: act like long‑term owners, adapt to a changing world, and build a company its people are proud of. The firm emphasizes supply‑chain resilience, noting that its manufacturing expertise lets customers get products when they need them, regardless of geopolitical conditions.

The business serves both retail customers and wholesale clients, though facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not disclosed.

Customers span individual consumers of all ages — wearing items at home, the gym, school, workplaces, and college campuses — as well as businesses and nonprofits seeking merchandise. One cited client, PGD Innovations, a nonprofit, relies on The Factory 10 for all its merchandise, including pricing, fabric selection, and design guidance.

The company states its mission rests on three pillars: empowerment, sustainability, and social impact. It emphasizes inclusive designs, eco-friendly practices, and collaborations with local artisans and marginalized communities. A portion of profits supports charitable organizations, and the company guarantees certified quality products with immediate replacement if unsatisfied.
